reviews.review: I recently replayed this since Soace Marine 2 is coming out and it still holds up in 2022. Multiplayer is kinda dead of course and the price is too high for the short campaign that has no replay value, Just pick it up in a sale.

with a good atmosphere nice gameplay and interesting story this is one of the better warhammer 40k games i have played. the Multiplayer is not very good but i have seen worse in my time of gaming. overal i would suggest getting this game in a sale or humblebundle for a cheap price.
Sadly there wont be any follow up games... i would have loved to know what happens to Titus and the ultramarines.

It feels Like gears of war mixed with a spectical fighter. 

As a third person action game it is fun, but for a non fan boy that is the extent of the package. I was thinking during the opening scene when you are jumping from your ship and falling towards ork ships how amazing it would be if you were in complete control, jumping from ship to ship to take them down. I was disapointed to find it was just an arena fight, followed by arena fights.

Not that it is bad, just nothing to expand on the formula.

Even counting the entire Dawn of War series, this is probably my favorite Warhammer 40K game.

The single player campaign is rock-solid. It's not going to knock your socks off in terms of narrative depth, but it absolutely nails the look and feel of WH40K.

This game covers all of the Warhammer 40K bases. You fight Orks. You fight the forces of Chaos. You blow things up and you kill tons of bad guys.

When you get to multiplayer, you have a wealth of options in terms of weaponry and armor. You can choose paint schemes from the old tabletop and miniatures games, or you can create your own. Armor comes in sets, but you can mix and match the pieces to create a space marine who looks just the way you want.

Loadouts are made up of a class, a weapon, a backup, and some perks. Each class has its own built-in abilities, but it is your weapon and your perks that really dial in your playstyle.

The Assault gets a jetpack, and it's just as fun to use as it looks and sounds. The Devastator gets the heavy and long range weaponry. They have high damage potential and can be a little tougher than the other two classes at the cost of being a little slower. The tactical marine is surprisingly maneuverable, and falls somewhere in between the other two. Not quite as mobile as the Assault, not quite as tough or as good at long range as the Devastator.

There's a nice balance to the multiplayer, though the population is pretty low this far out from release. Also, there's often "that guy" you'll run into with a cheap, super effective, or heavily-practised loadout. The early matches in multiplayer can be a bit rough due to some of those cheap and/or veteran players combined with most of the gear and perks not being unlocked yet. If you stick with it a little bit, you'll unlock more of the equipment and you'll find your niche. There are definitely certain playstyles that hard-counter others, but for the most part teamwork and positioning matter more than the gear you bring.

The only issue specific to PC multiplayer is the effectiveness of sniper-type weapons. They weren't used much console-side and still have their drawbacks, but with mice being so accurate some of the sniper-style weapons have become way more effective in PvP than they really should be. It's not often a problem, but on certain maps you may find yourself being killed from across the map or at any range as soon as they spot you; due to the ease with which they can hit you. Space Marines are big, bulky, and a bit slow. Most of the combat is designed around this, but players using these sniper-type weapons will often find the nearest vantage point and begin mercilessly destroying you and your team at all ranges. Sometimes, sneaking up on them isn't even enough. If they spot you coming up on them or if you don't kill them before they realize you're there, they can fire just as accurately at close range as long range (even if most of the other weapons outperform in speed or raw damage). It's annoying, and so are some of the Assault players when they catch you alone, but those are hardly deal-breakers.

If you decide to purchase this game, do it for the excellent single-player campaign and the co-op horde mode (which you can play solo and can use to farm some of the weapon challenges). "Annihilation" mode sometimes has players, and it can be very fun, but it's more of a nice bonus than a guarantee.
